title: Isandro and the Clock
premise: In 1917, Elodie Winterbourne drives for suffragist organizer Marguerite Ash and secretly reads every letter that passes through their hands, keeping a private ledger of names—women arrested, dismissed, disappeared. When the army requisitions the town and seizes the ledger as evidence of sedition, Elodie realizes the names will be used to prosecute the very people she has come to love as family. Copying the ledger by lamplight, Elodie and Marguerite's circle plan to smuggle the evidence past three military checkpoints to a journalist waiting across the river before the spring ice breaks. Elodie is caught at the final checkpoint but the ledger reaches print anyway, forcing a public trial where testimony from the named women turns the prosecution into an indictment of the army itself—and Elodie, once invisible, chooses to stand in the open and sign their own name.
about_author: Jude Oyelaran is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing wartime correspondence in regional collections across northern England. Their fiction explores how ordinary people keep records when institutions refuse to.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. We meet Elodie driving Marguerite through a snowbound mill town, reading letters at night and recording names in a hidden ledger—the arrested weaver's wife, the dismissed schoolteacher. The army arrives with requisition orders. Emotional beat: quiet belonging found in secret knowledge, shadowed by the first knock of state power at the door.

chapters.title: The Ledger Goes Dark
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Soldiers seize the meeting hall and confiscate the ledger; Marguerite is detained 'for questioning.' Elodie, spared because they are seen as merely staff, begins copying the names from memory each night while pretending loyalty to the garrison. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve—the moment invisibility becomes a weapon rather than a shelter.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Elodie and young soldier Tomas, who guards the second checkpoint and begins doubting his orders after recognizing a name on a wanted list. The smuggling attempt unravels: the first checkpoint passes them, the second nearly breaks them, and at the third Elodie is caught with the copy sewn into a coat lining. Emotional beat: rising dread and the fragile alliance between strangers.

chapters.title: Before the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, with interludes from the trial. The ledger reaches the journalist via Tomas's defection; the published names force a public hearing where the women testify. Facing charges, Elodie refuses anonymity and signs their own name in court. Emotional beat: catharsis and transformation—from reader of other people's letters to author of their own record, held fast by found family as the river finally thaws.
